posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
![Image](http://www.dragonseye.com/blog/uploads/holography/2005_04/04060017.jpg)

[edited to include a better photograph. It's a bit blown out but you get a better sense of the brightness and some of the clarity]

That is a hologram I'm doing for a co-worker of his Minas Tirith model from LOTR. It's a great model for holography as it's got tons of detail.

[http://www.dragonseye.com/blog/archives ... irith.html](http://www.dragonseye.com/blog/archives/28-Minas-Tirith.html)

Vital Statistics:

un-treated PFG-01 film exposed HeNe for 30 seconds.

Developed 50 seconds in JD2, bleached with EDTA

Lit with a 20W halogen

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md: That IS a nice subject. Holo size is 4x5? I assume it's an H2.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md: Yes, that is an H2 shot on 4x5". The final will be shot on 5x7" film for easier matting and framing.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: Very nice. Are you going to do a contact copy or another H2 transfer for the 5x7? Also, where is it and the final going to be image planed?

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
![Image](http://www.dragonseye.com/blog/uploads/holography/2005_04/04060029.jpg)

Here's a shot of the color test I did yesterday. Later today I'll upload the green version I did this morning.

The TEA %'s are 3.75 & 1.25 from left to right. 5% gives me a nice emerald green.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
> **JohnFP:** Very nice. Are you going to do a contact copy or another H2 transfer for the 5x7?

Thanks. It'll be another H2 transfer. It's easiest for me to leave the setup as-is rather than change it for a contact copy (something I'll have to try someday).

> **JohnFP:** Also, where is it and the final going to be image planed?

Look at the image at the front, lowest level. See the first wall with the window-looking thing at the top (it's behind and to the left of the gate)? The film plane cuts right through that wall and up through the ship's prow (that's what the pointy bit is meant to represent, but LOTR geeks should already know this ).

Part of the image comes out 1" in front of the plate.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: WOW! The gold is simply stunning.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
Yeah, the gold is nice. It goes well with the overall stone look too. I find as I look at all the colors that I like, well... them all. 

Here's the green shot I promised and a silly shot with a DCG next to it.
